items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: playtest list and design form)
items.title: A mine costs six months of net at the opening; ease over 10-20 years through reinvestment
items.design: Playtest item 20, Ben's most important. Ruling (Ben, 2026-11-05) in the authority doc. Target: a mine costs about 6 months of a major's net at the opening, back to about 1 month after 10-20 years; 6x in 15 years is about 13% a year, or roughly an 8-year payback on a good building. Cost lives mostly in materials, so a planned steel chain is the edge. Good sites pay back in years, poor ones barely: the finder stays open (Ben declined gating it), so this spread is the WHOLE reward for searching and must be read, not assumed. Calibrate from the payback census; multipliers are in-band. RISKS: raises steel demand and can stretch or pause sites (max_stretch); rivals barely build today (median 44 to about 47 in five years), so read whether they stall further; read against BL-1494 (tick-50 stall). Check: market-viability, opening-parity, rebless-shape-probe. One re-bless shared with the other world-movers. CALIBRATION from the census (BL-1496): six months of net at the measured 1,000-1,150 a quarter is a mine of about 2,000-2,300, about 5-6x today's 327-430. Reinvestment grows income at 1/payback whatever the net: a x5.5 mine pays back in about 5 years on produce (0.9 today), 9 on copper, 21 on iron, 40 on coal; standing processors in about 15-25 years. Background growth of about 4.7% a year carries about 2.5x of the 6x over 20 years, leaving about 2.4x for reinvestment, so x5-6 looks feasible and must be run, not assumed. Timber, fibre and stone mines cost about 105-110 today with no steel in the bill: the materials lever must reach them. Read net after research: see the review queue.

items.design: SPACE_ASSETS.md § Launching: a launch needs a staffed Launchpad on the nation home body. placement_rules allows one Launchpad per body world-wide; make it one per nation per body. The nation build scorer (2026-10-23 grant, own ground only) builds a Launchpad once the nation holds Rocketry and can afford it, and an Astronaut Training Centre once it holds the training key; never for the player. Done when a spectated run shows rivals launching (the spectate census reports launches). Outcome (lane Q, seed 0 to 1995): pads and centres built (first pad 1977, 4 staffed by 1995), but 0 launches: the launch lots are not on the home shelf (BL-1630, launch goods supply).

items.author: Claude (spectator finding, BL-1615)
items.title: Rivals with a staffed pad can buy a launch: spacecraft components and propellant reach the home shelf, and pads finish in reasonable time
items.design: The BL-1615 spectate (seed 0 to 1995) ends with 4 staffed rival pads and 0 launches. Three padded nations are refused rejected_shelf: their home market holds no spacecraft_components or propellant lot (components_lump 25, propellant_lump 50), though treasuries are 50 to 88k. The plants exist (recipes spacecraft_components, spacecraft_components_heavy, propellant_atmospheric) but nothing builds them: no demand shows before a launch. Second gap: pads take 5 to 9 years, some sites at rate 0 for want of materials. Fix as an in-world force, not a term in the agent: the space programme demand must be visible to the nation build scorer (2026-10-23 grant, own ground only) so it builds the plants, or the launch buy must post a standing order the market and builders can see. Done when a spectated run shows rival launches before 2000.

items.author: Claude (BL-1602 lane report)
items.title: A garrison defending its province can chase a pushing stack forever without a battle
items.design: Seen on any body: the lower-id attacker steps first each day, the push prefers empty tiles, and the defender walks onto the tile the attacker just left, so they never meet. war_bodies_harness clears the defend order before its battle to avoid it. Diagnose the step order and fix so a defender closing on a pusher meets it.
